response.justification: Strong, versatile engineer with genuine geospatial domain experience (GISCollective, Green Map web GIS) and some high-throughput systems work in D at Sociomantic/dunnhumby (async I/O, fibers, caching, millions of req/s). However, the role's primary requirement — modern C++ (or Rust) in commercial or open-source settings — is essentially unmet: C/C++ appears only in a 7-month role at National Instruments over a decade ago and a university thesis project. The last decade is predominantly TypeScript/Node full-stack and web platform work, with no evidence of routing/tiling, map data pipelines, or large-scale distributed data infrastructure. Could be worth a screening call given the geospatial passion and demonstrated ability to learn new stacks, but there is a substantial ramp-up risk for a mid-senior IC expected to own critical pipeline components.
strengths: Real geospatial/GIS product experience via GISCollective and Green Map
Low-latency, high-volume backend work with async I/O and caching at Sociomantic
Proven polyglot adaptability, strong testing/TDD and CI/CD discipline
concerns: No recent modern C++ or any Rust experience (C/C++ last used ~2015)
Recent decade is web/full-stack TypeScript, not systems or data pipelines
No evidence of routing, tiling, or large-scale distributed data infrastructure
